title: Otis Announces Global Winners in 2026 Made to Move Communities™ Challenge
content:
Students from schools in Athens, Greece and Hong Kong SAR win STEM and AI competition with concepts to help people during natural disasters

FARMINGTON, Conn., May 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- With their ideas to use advanced technology to support city officials, first responders and residents before and during natural disasters, student teams from Hong Kong and Athens, Greece were named co‑champions of Otis' Made to Move Communities™ student challenge, in recognition of the exceptional strength and impact of both teams' solutions. Otis (NYSE: OTIS) is the world's leading elevator and escalator manufacturing, installation, service and modernization company.Students from HKFYG Lee Shau Kee College in Hong Kong SAR and Geniko Lyceum Filothei in Athens, Greece are global co-champions in this year’s Otis Made to Move Communities challenge, with their concepts to use advanced technology to support city officials, first responders and residents before and during natural disasters.

"Congratulations to the student teams from and HKFYG Lee Shau Kee College and Geniko Lyceum Filothei, this year's co‑champions of our Made to Move Communities global challenge. Their projects reflect not only technical ingenuity and creativity, but also a clear focus on helping vulnerable communities and first responders when it matters most," said Randi Tanguay, Otis Chief Communications Officer. "The students — with support from their mentors — demonstrate the confidence and capability of a new generation, ready to apply technology with thoughtfulness and purpose. We hope they continue exploring, identifying challenges, and finding ways to use technology to help their communities connect and thrive."

About this year's challenge: A focus on natural disasters

The annual Made to Move Communities program inspires students to address real-world mobility challenges aligned with global trends and areas where Otis' business expertise can make meaningful impact. This year's theme focused on natural disasters, as students applied STEM skills and AI-driven thinking to develop mobility solutions to help vulnerable populations and first responders react to increasingly frequent and severe events.

The team from Geniko Lyceum Filothei in Filothei, Athens, Greece developed a concept for an AI-enabled container that tracks rainfall fluctuation and resultant water levels and activates a preventive response system to alert local emergency management personnel and protect vulnerable residents during flood risk events.

The team from HKFYG Lee Shau Kee College in Hong Kong SAR developed a concept for a combined AI and augmented reality system to help first responders see and stay connected in smoke-filled, low-visibility situations.

More than 200 high school students from 18 schools in 14 countries and territories participated in this year's Made to Move Communities challenge.

Story Continues

Continuing STEM education

As global co-champions, the students at HKFYG Lee Shau Kee College and Geniko Lyceum Filothei earned $35,000 in grants for each of their respective schools.

"This achievement reflects the creativity, curiosity and hard work our students bring to everything they do," said Lin Chun Pong, Principal of HKFYG Lee Shau Kee College. "They've transformed classroom learning into a practical solution with the potential to address real challenges beyond our school walls, and that's an experience that will stay with them. We are incredibly proud of their accomplishment."

"It has been inspiring to watch these students grow and apply technical and critical‑thinking skills to real‑world challenges," said Petros Matzakos, Principal of Geniko Lyceum Filothei. "We are incredibly proud of their achievement and thankful to our staff and the Otis volunteer mentors who made this experience — and future opportunities — possible."

To learn more about the Made to Move Communities program, visit www.otis.com/mtmc.

What is the Otis Made to Move Communities program?

Otis' Made to Move Communities™ program is the company's flagship social impact program. It is a global student challenge inspiring creative, STEM- and AI-based solutions to real-world mobility issues.

Over the past several months, the student teams worked alongside more than 150 Otis mentors to develop and refine their concepts, presenting them to panels of Otis judges across the company's four regions: Americas, Asia Pacific, Greater China and EMEA (Europe, Middle East & Africa). Four regional winners then went on to compete in a final, global competition, judged by members of the Otis Executive Leadership Team.

What are the goals of the Made to Move Communities program?

The Made to Move Communities program brings together students, educators and Otis colleagues as mentors, with the goals of advancing STEM and leadership skills to help build the next generation of talent, ensuring future workforce readiness and sustaining innovation.

What is the community impact of the Made to Move Communities program?

Since 2020, Made to Move Communities has engaged over 1,000 Otis colleagues in mentoring more than 1,250 students, and delivered 145 grants totaling nearly $1.5 million to support ongoing STEM education at participating schools.

Why is the Made to Move Communities program focused on natural disasters this year?

Each year, Otis identifies a theme grounded in global trends and areas where its business expertise can make meaningful impact, such as aging populations, accessibility or emerging technology.

Otis chose this year's theme as over the past half century, natural disasters have increased in frequency at least five-fold and have also become more intense. Disasters can often lead to or exacerbate human mobility challenges, vulnerabilities and needs among affected communities, including by first responders.

About Otis

Otis gives people freedom to connect and thrive in a taller, faster, smarter world. The global leader in the manufacture, installation, service and modernization of elevators and escalators, we move 2.5 billion people a day and maintain approximately 2.5 million customer units worldwide — the industry's largest Service portfolio. You'll find us in the world's most iconic structures, as well as residential and commercial buildings, transportation hubs and everywhere people are on the move. Headquartered in Connecticut, USA, Otis is 72,000 people strong, including 45,000 field professionals, all committed to manufacturing, installing and maintaining products to meet the diverse needs of our customers and passengers in more than 200 countries and territories. To learn more, visit www.otis.com and follow us on LinkedIn, YouTube, Instagram and Facebook @OtisElevatorCo.

title: 3 Reasons to Sell OTIS and 1 Stock to Buy Instead
content:
Over the past six months, Otis’s shares (currently trading at $77.13) have posted a disappointing 15% loss, well below the S&P 500’s 6.4% gain. This may have investors wondering how to approach the situation.

Is now the time to buy Otis, or should you be careful about including it in your portfolio? Get the full stock story straight from our expert analysts, it’s free.

Why Do We Think Otis Will Underperform?

Even with the cheaper entry price, we don't have much confidence in Otis. Here are three reasons why OTIS doesn't excite us and a stock we'd rather own.

1. Core Business Falling Behind as Demand Plateaus

In addition to reported revenue, organic revenue is a useful data point for analyzing General Industrial Machinery companies. This metric gives visibility into Otis’s core business because it excludes one-time events such as mergers, acquisitions, and divestitures along with foreign currency fluctuations - non-fundamental factors that can manipulate the income statement.

Over the last two years, Otis failed to grow its organic revenue. This performance was underwhelming and implies it may need to improve its products, pricing, or go-to-market strategy. It also suggests Otis might have to lean into acquisitions to accelerate growth, which isn’t ideal because M&A can be expensive and risky (integrations often disrupt focus).Otis Organic Revenue Growth

2. Projected Revenue Growth Is Slim

Forecasted revenues by Wall Street analysts signal a company’s potential. Predictions may not always be accurate, but accelerating growth typically boosts valuation multiples and stock prices while slowing growth does the opposite.

Over the next 12 months, sell-side analysts expect Otis’s revenue to rise by 4.4%. Although this projection suggests its newer products and services will catalyze better top-line performance, it is still below the sector average.

3. Recent EPS Growth Below Our Standards

While long-term earnings trends give us the big picture, we also track EPS over a shorter period because it can provide insight into an emerging theme or development for the business.

Otis’s EPS grew at an unimpressive 5.4% compounded annual growth rate over the last two years. On the bright side, this performance was higher than its 1.2% annualized revenue growth and tells us the company became more profitable on a per-share basis as it expanded.Otis Trailing 12-Month EPS (Non-GAAP)

Final Judgment

Otis falls short of our quality standards. Following the recent decline, the stock trades at 18.3× forward P/E (or $77.13 per share). This valuation tells us a lot of optimism is priced in - we think other companies feature superior fundamentals at the moment. Let us point you toward the Amazon and PayPal of Latin America.

title: Generac Tops Q1 Earnings Estimates, Lifts 2026 Revenue Outlook
content:
Generac Holdings Inc. GNRC reported first-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.80, which beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.33. GNRC registered an adjusted EPS of $1.26 in the prior-year quarter.

Net sales were $1.06 billion, up 12% from $942 million in the prior-year quarter. The figure also beat the consensus estimate of nearly $1.044 billion. Strength in the Commercial & Industrial (“C&I”) segment, especially the data center market, acted as a catalyst. Generac added that it was in the final stages of vendor approval with several hyperscale customers. It is also witnessing backlog expansion for these products with both current and new customers. The Enercon buyout (completed earlier this month) is expected to boost GNRC’s vertical integration and support margin expansion for megawatt backup power offerings.

Given the strong first-quarter performance and momentum in the data center market and increasing backlog, GNRC now expects 2026 revenues to increase in the mid-to-high teens percent range. This includes a 2% positive impact from the net effect of foreign currency, acquisitions and divestitures. The earlier growth target was in the mid-teens percent range.

Generac Holdings Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS SurpriseGenerac Holdings Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Generac Holdings Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Generac Holdings Inc. Quote

C&I product sales are anticipated to increase in the mid-to-high 20% range compared with the earlier target of low-to-mid 20% range. Residential product sales are expected to increase in the 10% range for 2026. 

The net income margin (before deducting for non-controlling interests) is expected to be between 8% and 9%. The adjusted EBITDA margin is estimated to be 18.5-19.5% as compared with the earlier guided range of 18-19%.Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

GNRC is up 8.6% in the pre-market trading today. The stock has gained 89.8% compared with the Manufacturing-General Industrial industry’s growth of 24.9% in the past year.

GNRC’s Segments in Detail

Beginning from the first quarter of 2026, Generac's two reportable segments are now Residential and C&I. 

The Residential segment consists of the former Domestic segment minus the domestic C&I operations. The C&I segment consists of the former International segment, plus the domestic C&I operations. 

Revenues from Residential were up 1% year over year to $552.2 million, driven by higher portable generator shipments, partially offset by reduced energy storage system sales. Sales of home standby generators remained unchanged from the prior-year quarter as higher pricing offset reduced volumes. 

C&I revenues totaled $510.1 million, up 28% year over year. This included 10% net favorable impact from the combination of acquisitions, divestitures and foreign currency. The core revenue growth for the segment was driven by higher sales to data center customers and shipments to domestic industrial distributors and rental channels. Increasing sales of the control solutions to the power generation vertical acted as another tailwind. 

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Residential and C&I products’ first-quarter revenues was pegged at $518 million and $439 million, respectively.

Story Continues

GNRC’s Margin Performance

Gross profit was $410.2 million, up from nearly $372 million in the prior-year quarter, with respective margins of 38.7% and 39.5%. The margin performance was impacted by an unfavorable sales mix, which offset higher price realization. 

Total operating expenses were $292.9 million, up 2% year over year, caused by higher intangible amortization.

The operating income was $117.3 million compared with $83.6 million in the prior-year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA, before deducting for non-controlling interests, was $193 million compared with $150 million a year ago.

GNRC’s Cash Flow & Liquidity

In the first quarter, the company generated $119 million of net cash from operating activities. The free cash flow totaled $90 million.

As of March 31, 2025, GNRC had $265.5 million of cash and cash equivalents, with $1.25 billion of long-term borrowings and finance-lease obligations. 

The company did not buy back stock in the first quarter. In 2025, the company repurchased 1.1 million shares for $148 million. GNRC also earlier approved a share repurchase authorization of up to $500 million over the next 24 months. This new program replaces the remaining balance of the earlier program.

GNRC’s Zacks Rank

Generac currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Recent Performances of Other Companies in the Same Space

Otis Worldwide Corporation OTIS reported mixed first-quarter 2026 results. Earnings per share (EPS) of 89 cents missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 91 cents by 2.2%. In the year-ago quarter, it reported an adjusted EPS of 92 cents.

OTIS’ net sales of $3.57 billion surpassed the consensus mark of $3.5 billion by 2% and increased 6.4% on a year-over-year basis. Organically, net sales were up 1% year over year. Favorable foreign exchange movement supported sales growth by 5%. A standout in the quarter was repair, with net sales up 16% at actual currency and organic repair sales up about 10%.

Dover Corporation DOV posted first-quarter fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of $2.28 per share, up 11.2% from $2.05 a year ago. The figure topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.27, reflecting a 0.4% surprise.

Dover Corporation’s quarterly revenues rose 10.1% year over year to $2.05 billion, beating the consensus mark of $2.01 billion by 2.1%. The upside was backed by solid growth in secular-growth-exposed end markets and improving conditions across DOV’s portfolio. Excellent order activity, with book-to-bill above one across all five segments, aided growth.

Graco Inc.’s GGG first-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of 66 cents per share were down 6% from 70 cents in the year-ago quarter. The bottom line missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 75 cents by 12%.

Graco’s net sales rose 2% year over year to $540.1 million but lagged the consensus estimate of $560 million by 3.5%. Organic order backlog rose 13% from the end of 2025. On a regional basis, quarterly sales generated from the Americas increased 3% year over year. In Europe, the Middle East and Africa, sales increased 4% year over year. Sales from the Asia Pacific decreased 5% year over year.

title: How elevator operator Otis is capitalizing on the AI boom
content:
Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi welcomes Otis Worldwide Corporation (OTIS) CEO Judy Marks on Opening Bid. Marks reveals how the 150+ year-old elevator brand is shifting with the times and surging alongside the boom in AI data center projects.

Video Transcript

00:00 Speaker A

Well, certainly we're an AI user as is as is any company and I'm sure you can't have a CEO on here not talking about how it's impacting and transforming our business. But for us, uh the data centers are are a large demand signal we're seeing right now. Uh it's in the US where it's the largest demand, but we're seeing it everywhere. So we introduced a new heavy industrial product. It's uh it's it's amazing. It's got extra vibration shock to handle, handle critical infrastructure when you're moving racks and servers.

00:25 Speaker B

It's expensive.

00:26 Speaker A

Well, it it's it's priced well for being immediately available and for being very robust and we call it our robust line. So it does everything from uh moving people, but more importantly, we've designed it extra wide, extra wide door openings, but for a smooth ride and for 24/7 availability, which is what the data centers need.

00:41 Speaker B

I thought these data centers were one floor. I didn't realize they were now spanning multiple floors.

00:43 Speaker A

Yeah, so whether it's a data center or any of the new chip manufacturing facilities, all the reshoring that's going on in this comp- in this country for manufacturing, they're usually now more than one story just like the e-commerce sites. Uh because you they just can't take up as much land as they used to. So that ability to move, move pa- move servers around, to move equipment around. Uh and again, to be able to do that reliably, we can plug into backup power, they're connected. So again, that ultimate availability, 24/7, and also the availability of our elevators immediately so that we continue the construction boom that's happening.

01:07 Speaker B

Uh, this is a boom in this country, no question about it. Can you make enough of these specialized elevators to service the demand you're seeing?

01:12 Speaker A

We absolutely can and you know, we've we've taken from our common product platform, the ability to build them very quickly, very rapidly. We've trained trained our installation teams, and then we'll service them for as long as the data centers are there. So, people think about are there really jobs in data centers? There absolutely are, uh beyond just the operation, but making sure they stay up and running.

01:28 Speaker B

Every day there's a new wrinkle to this AI story. Today, it's the Wall Street Journal talking about Open AI and maybe missing some targets. But like you are in the trenches. You sit on the board of a Caterpillar. Caterpillar has trucks like dump trucks like helping to dig the sites, elevators. How do you see this this outlook for the AI infrastructure demand, uh looking out over the next 24 months, for example?

01:41 Speaker A

Well, in the US, it's going to be tremendously strong. I mean, people's backlogs are getting filled, but I mean, we're seeing an even stronger demand signal across all of the US for buildings. And I think that takes people back a little. We've had our seventh straight quarter of new equipment orders growth over 25% in the US. Uh and then the refurbishment of buildings, cuz buildings, you know, they need to be refurbished, they need to stay alive. They've been constructed 20 and 30 years ago. And so our modernization refurbishment orders in the US are up 35% this quarter. So we're just uh we're we're trying to meet this demand where it is, whether it's in residential, whether it's in hospitals, manufacturing, data centers, the the beauty of elevators and what we do is they're ubiquitous. Anytime you're two stories or more, you need us, people don't think about us that much.

02:12 Speaker B

Yeah, we're not climbing up the outside of the building like Spider-Man. That's not how this goes.

02:15 Speaker A

And then infrastructure's growing, stadiums, airports, you think about what's going on in this country and we're really positive.

title: Conflict in Middle East weighs on company coffers, clouds outlook
content:
As first-quarter earnings gather pace, companies from luxury retailers to travel and industrial giants are flagging warnings on the financial impact of the ongoing U.S.-Israel war with Iran on their balance sheet.

Despite hopes for robust ​first-quarter earnings, several companies so far have either cut guidance or issued financial warnings, underscoring rising pressure on their operations. The caution comes amid higher oil prices, ongoing supply chain disruptions, softer consumer confidence, and slowing growth, all of which are clouding their forecasts.

Already weighed down by tariff headwinds, companies are now facing fresh worries stemming from the ongoing Middle East conflict.

“Many U.S. and European companies are still reporting solid numbers, but the tone on earnings calls is clearly shifting. The issue is not necessarily demand today; it is the difficulty of forecasting costs, supply chains, energy prices, consumer confidence and investment decisions over the next few quarters,” said PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore.

U.S. industrial giant HONEYWELL (HON [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/HON]) on Thursday forecast second-quarter ‌revenue below Wall Street estimates, citing the Middle East conflict. Honeywell CEO Vimal Kapur told analysts the conflict caused a 0.5% reduction in revenue during the first quarter and that he expects ​roughly a 1% drop during the second quarter, largely in its process automation and technology segment.

“The loss of revenue we're having in Middle East is also high-margin revenue. So that just has associated margin pressure because of services software, which is impacted the most due to disruptions there,” Kapur said.

Aluminium maker ALCOA (AA [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AA]) said [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4576192-alcoa-slides-on-q1-miss-as-alumina-weakness-disruptions-weigh-on-results-and-outlook] in the second-quarter, it expects the conflict in Iran to contribute to an unfavorable impact of $15M on adjusted EBITDA in its alumina segment. Earlier this month, oilfield services firm NOV (NOV [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/NOV]) also warned [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4575166-nov-sees-q1-revenues-earnings-below-prior-guidance-on-middle-east-war-disruptions] that operational disruptions resulting from the Middle East war will weigh on its first quarter.

Oilfield services contractor HALLIBURTON’S (HAL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/HAL]) COO Jeffrey Slocum emphasized on operational disruption saying “activity has been most impacted in the region's offshore markets in Qatar, UAE, Saudi Arabia and the land markets in Iraq and Kuwait” and outlined Q2 conflict impact [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4577406-halliburton-outlines-q2-conflict-impact-of-0_07-to-0_09-per-share-while-holding-2026-capex-at] of $0.07 to $0.09 per share.

Activity has been most impacted in the region's offshore markets in Qatar, UAE, Saudi Arabia and the land markets in Iraq and Kuwait

Several companies, during earnings calls, stressed on the fact that disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical corridor for global oil supplies, has led to decreased visibility. TAIWAN SEMICONDUCTOR MANUFACTURING (TSM [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/TSM]) warned [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4891129-taiwan-semiconductor-manufacturing-company-limited-tsm-q1-2026-earnings-call-transcript] higher prices for gas and chemicals due to the conflict could impact profitability. However, the chipmaker added it is too early to quantify the impact.

Similarly, JINKOSOLAR (JKS [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/JKS]) said the conflict will have [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4891263-jinkosolar-holding-co-ltd-jks-q4-2025-earnings-call-transcript] an impact on its shipment to the Middle East, even though the impact won’t be long-term. Industrial giant 3M (MMM [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/MMM]) warned of about $125 million worth of annual cost impact [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4892411-3m-company-mmm-q1-2026-earnings-call-transcript] due to higher oil prices.

Elevator maker OTIS WORLDWIDE (OTIS [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/OTIS]) said it experienced modernization project delays in EMEA due to the conflict in the first quarter. The company, however, believes [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4892870-otis-worldwide-corporation-otis-q1-2026-earnings-call-transcript] that these delays are recoverable through the remainder of the year.

Several executives raised concern regarding the escalation of the war and tried to evaluate and explain the financial hit to their businesses.

DOW (DOW [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/DOW]) used its first-quarter earnings call to deliver a blunt message [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4579006-dow-warns-strait-of-hormuz-disruption-could-lift-costs-through-2026] to analysts: the conflict involving the U.S. and Iran, and the resulting disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, is no short-term nuisance, and it could lift costs through 2026.

Shares of SERVICENOW (NOW [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/NOW]) closed over 17% down after reporting that its first-quarter results were dented by delays in the Middle East. The company’s subscription revenue grew 19% in the quarter, but included a 75 basis point headwind [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4893100-servicenow-inc-now-q1-2026-earnings-call-transcript] from delayed closings of several large on-premise deals in the Middle East due to the conflict.

TRAVEL STOCKS TAKE A HIT

A surge in the jet fuel prices have already led to airlines companies hiking costs for checked-in baggage. Now, with these companies releasing quarterly results, investors are getting a clearer view of the financial impacts.

U.S. carrier UNITED AIRLINES (UAL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/UAL]) spooked the market after lowering its profit outlook [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4578145-united-airlines-cuts-2026-forecast-on-fuel-costs-ranks-only-fifth-among-us-airlines-by-quant], while ALASKA AIR (ALK [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ALK]) suspended [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4577073-alaska-air-points-to-strong-underlying-demand-despite-fuel-and-weather-challenges] full-year guidance due to the uncertainty around higher fuel costs. AMERICAN AIRLINES (AAL [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/AAL]) also cut [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4578672-american-airlines-generates-record-revenue-sees-price-hikes-offsetting-fuel-costs-in-fy26] its 2026 profit forecast.

GE AEROSPACE (GE [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/GE]), a key supplier to airlines, gave a full-year earnings guidance that remained below consensus despite management’s upbeat tone. The Ohio-based company’s CEO Larry Culp told [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/ge-aerospace-sees-2026-profit-top-range-warns-oil-risks-2026-04-21/] Reuters the company would have raised its forecast if not for the ​current uncertainty.

LUFTHANSA (DLAKF [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/DLAKF]) said it will remove 20,000 short-haul flights [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4578423-lufthansa-cuts-20000-unprofitable-flights-to-save-on-jet-fuel-costs] through October as a result of jet fuel prices doubling since the outbreak of the Iran war.

[Seeking ALpha]
Crude prices jumped due to the war, leading to IEA chief warning that the world faces biggest energy security threat in history (Seeking Alpha) 

EUROPE’S LUXURY FIRMS IN DISTRESS

With the global luxury industry already grappling with slowing growth, deteriorating spending by shoppers, especially in the Gulf areas, caused by the conflict has now dented hopes for a recovery in luxury demand.

French luxury goods group LVMH MOËT HENNESSY LOUIS VUITTON (LVMHF [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/LVMHF]) posted a 6% decline in quarterly sales [https://seekingalpha.com/news/4574512-lvmh-moet-hennessy-q1-revenue-slips-6-as-middle-east-conflict-weighs-on-luxury-sales], with the conflict having a 1% negative impact on organic growth.

LVMH's finance chief Cecile Cabanis said [https://seekingalpha.com/article/4890679-lvmh-moet-hennessy-louis-vuitton-societe-europeenne-lv-ca-q1-2026-sales-trading-call] mall traffic in the Middle ‌East ⁠accounts for about 6% of group turnover.

“When the conflict started, and in the month of March, there was a shortfall and a deterioration of demand between 30% and 70%, depending on the malls, depending on the businesses,” Cabanis added.

KERING (PPRUF [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/PPRUF]) said first-quarter sales ​at its Italian flagship brand Gucci dropped more than ‌expected, while Birkin bag maker HERMÈS INTERNATIONAL’S (HESAY [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/HESAY]) (HESAF [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/HESAF]) sales in the Middle East, its fastest-growing region in 2025, were down 6%.

Other European stocks also showed concerns.

Britain's top food retailer TESCO (TSCDY [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/TSCDY]) warned that profits could fall amid war uncertainty. Airline company EASYJET (EJTTF [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/EJTTF]) (ESYJY [https://seekingalpha.com/symbol/ESYJY]) reportedly said the Iran war and higher fuel prices are weighing on customer bookings.

With more companies preparing to post quarterly earnings, investors and analysts will be closely watching how this conflict unfolds in the upcoming weeks—and how businesses plan to navigate and mitigate the resulting financial pressures.

“Investors have likely priced in some near-term disruption, particularly in oil, freight and travel. What is less priced in is duration. If this remains contained, markets will look through many of these warnings. But if disruption persists for several quarters, guidance cuts will start to matter far more, especially for companies with weak pricing power or high exposure to energy, logistics and discretionary spending,” added Pescatore.

title: Looking At The Shifting Narrative For Otis Worldwide (OTIS) As Valuation Assumptions Reset
content:
Track your investments for FREE with Simply Wall St, the portfolio command center trusted by over 7 million individual investors worldwide.

Otis Worldwide’s fair value estimate has been revised from US$101.64 to US$96.93, a trim that reflects a more measured stance on what investors might reasonably pay for the shares. This adjustment sits alongside mixed research views, where fresh bullish initiations and a series of target cuts both shape how the market is thinking about Otis’s long term appeal. As you read on, you will see how to interpret these shifting targets and keep track of the evolving narrative around the stock.

Analyst Price Targets don't always capture the full story. Head over to our Company Report to find new ways to value Otis Worldwide.

What Wall Street Has Been Saying

🐂 Bullish Takeaways

Evercore ISI and BNP Paribas have both started coverage with positive views, with BNP Paribas citing Otis Worldwide as its preferred way to get exposure to the elevator sector and setting a US$109 price target. These bullish initiations suggest some analysts see room for upside between current pricing assumptions and their view of what the business could be worth over time.

🐻 Bearish Takeaways

Several firms, including Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo and Barclays, have lowered their price targets, with Wells Fargo cutting by US$12 and Morgan Stanley by US$8. This indicates that more conservative expectations are built into their models. JPMorgan has taken a more cautious stance, downgrading Otis Worldwide and describing its previous thesis as broken after Q4. Wolfe Research also issued a downgrade during April, signaling concerns about execution or future growth drivers.

What's in the News

Otis issued revised full year 2026 guidance, with expected net sales in a range of US$15.1b to US$15.3b. The company reported progress on its share repurchase program, buying back 4,568,331 shares for US$400m in the first quarter of 2026, bringing total repurchases under the current plan to 12,096,331 shares for US$1,099.97m. The board declared a quarterly dividend of US$0.44 per share, described as a 5% increase, payable on June 12, 2026, to shareholders of record on May 15, 2026. Otis expanded its product lineup with the Otis Robust heavy duty elevator range for data centers and critical infrastructure, and introduced Arise MOD Prime and Arise MOD Plus modernization packages in North America for low to mid rise buildings.

How This Changes the Fair Value For Otis Worldwide

Fair value trimmed from US$101.64 to US$96.93. Assumed long term revenue growth adjusted from 4.83% to 4.72%. Long term net profit margin moved from 11.81% to 11.74%. Forward P/E multiple reduced from 24.83x to 23.47x. Discount rate shifted from 8.92% to 9.02%.
